Exceptional Education at the Heart of the Community
Oasis Academy Putney Closure
Oasis Academy Putney closed on 31 August 2026 and is no longer in operation.
If you have an enquiry relating to the closure of Oasis Academy Putney, please email queries.putney@oasisuk.org
If you are seeking support or advice about a child’s welfare, please contact Wandsworth Multi-Agency Safeguarding Hub at mash@wandsworth.gov.uk or 020 8871 6622.
If you believe a child is at immediate risk of harm, call 999. You can also find local support and contact details at Wandsworth's Family Information Service.
All pupil safeguarding records have been securely transferred and retained in accordance with statutory requirements. Requests relating to former pupil records should be directed to safeguarding@oasisuk.org

pageCache.pageTitle: Values and ethos - Oasis Community Learning
pageCache.text:
Exceptional Education at the Heart of the Community
Values and ethos
The overall vision for every part of Oasis is for community. A place where everyone is included, making a contribution and reaching their God-given potential. Delivering first-class, innovative education is part of the work we do as we seek to grow an Oasis Hub in every area where we work; creating safe and inspiring local neighbourhoods that provide integrated and diverse services to benefit the whole person and whole community.
Exceptional Education at the Heart of the Community
We understand the complex responsibilities of education, through a lens of character, competence and community. Underpinned by the Oasis Ethos and 9 Habits, all these are intentionally developed and embedded into all aspects of life in our academies shaping and impacting what happens each and every day.
We have a commitment to inclusion, social integration and closing the disadvantage gap; we want to give advantage to the disadvantaged. Through a fostering of character and relationships, we have a shared determination to learn and develop together so that we grow as one community; one family.
Together, Oasis staff aspire to:
Help children and young people to thrive at every layer of their lives – educationally, relationally, mentally, spiritually, environmentally, vocationally and physically - both now and in the future.
Create safe, stimulating learning environments where curiosity is celebrated
Increase progress and attainment above national averages
Provide high quality teaching which secures good and accelerated progress for all students
Our ethos
Everything within Oasis is framed by our ethos.
Our ethos is rooted in what we believe and who we are. Grounded in our story, it is an expression of our character; a set of values that inform and provide the lens on everything we do.
A passion to include
A desire to treat people equally respecting differences
A commitment to healthy, open relationships
A deep sense of hope that things can change and be transformed
A sense of perseverance to keep going for the long haul
It is these ethos values that we want to be known for and to live by. We are committed to a model of inclusion, equality, healthy relationships, hope, and perseverance throughout all the aspects of the life and culture of every Oasis Hub and academy community.
We encourage every member of our family, be that staff or student, to align themselves to these ethos values. The values themselves are Christ-centred, but we make it clear that we do not and will not impose the beliefs that underpin our ethos values on anyone. We recognise and celebrate the richness that spiritual and cultural diversity brings to our community, respecting the beliefs and practices of other faiths in the hope that we will provide a welcoming environment for all.
The Oasis 9 Habits
The Oasis Ethos is aspirational, inspirational and something that we have to constantly work at. It is important to remember that every organisation is made up of its people, and people don’t always get things right. This means that there can sometimes be a dissonance or disconnect between what we say we are, as stated in our ethos values, and what we actually do and experience.
Recognising this is helpful because it reminds us that we each have things to work on; we have space to grow, develop and change to become the best version of ourselves.
To help us in this process of personal growth and development we have the Oasis 9 Habits. It is our bespoke and unique approach to character development. We know that by living the way of the Habits, the Oasis Ethos will become second nature to us.
We also believe that this process of continually developing our character and being transformed to become the best version of ourselves is really important for every student and staff member alike. Therefore, we actively promote and practice the Oasis 9 Habits which are an invitation to a way of life characterised by being compassionate, patient, humble, joyful, honest, hopeful, considerate, forgiving and self-controlled.
We believe that by becoming people who live this way, by becoming the best version of ourselves, whether we are a staff member or students, we are transformed, and we are also able to play our part in bringing transformation locally, nationally and globally.
And this is who we are.

pageCache.pageTitle: Equity Through Inclusion - Oasis Community Learning
pageCache.text:
Exceptional Education at the Heart of the Community
Equity Through Inclusion
Equity, Difference and Belonging through Inclusion for All
At Oasis, we are committed to the equity and flourishing of all our people. This commitment is rooted in the foundational beliefs of our organisation and expressed through our ethos values: a passion to include and a desire to treat people equally while respecting differences.
These values are not abstract ideals; they shape the decisions we make and the way we live and work together. Guided by our ethos and the Oasis 9 Habits, we are continually developing our practices to become as inclusive as we can possibly be.
We work towards equity through:
• Listening and Learning – valuing staff voice through surveys and feedback
• Inclusive Governance – steering groups that monitor and challenge our practice
• Belonging Networks – including forums for gender equality, LGBTQ+, disabled, and ethnically diverse colleagues and community members
• Learning and Development – including training on unconscious bias, disability, inclusion, menopause, and anti-racism
• Policy and Practice – ensuring our governance, infrastructure, and working conditions reflect our commitment to fairness
• People Strategy – setting out how we value and invest in our staff
We recognise that true equity is only possible when everyone feels included, valued, and safe enough to bring their whole selves—to voice their experiences, express their differences, and participate fully in our shared life together.
Inclusion at Oasis is not an add-on—it is woven into our culture, our systems, and our future. From staff networks to Inclusion Champions, and from the voices of students to those of our communities, we are building a Trust-wide approach that ensures everyone feels inspired, enabled, and empowered to thrive.
We know inclusion is a journey. We are proud of the recognition our academies have received so far—and even more committed to exploring ways we can grow stronger together.
At Oasis, we believe that when everyone belongs, everyone flourishes.

Exceptional Education at the Heart of the Community
Welcome
A very warm welcome to Oasis Community Learning!
I am delighted that you are interested in finding out more about us. Oasis Community Learning was established as a Multi-Academy Trust in 2005 with the vision to create “Exceptional Education at the Heart of the Community”. We now run academies in five main regions throughout the UK, providing either Primary, Secondary or All-through education to over 32,000 young people - 47% of whom are from disadvantaged backgrounds and 31% speak English as an additional language.
All of our academies are committed to providing a rich educational experience and ensuring that every child and young person has the opportunity to achieve at the highest level. Our ethos is integral to that provision. It is an expression of our character, a statement of who we are and therefore the lens through which we assess all we do. We are committed to a model of inclusion, equality, healthy relationships, hope and perseverance throughout all aspects of the life and culture of each academy community.
We passionately embrace learning and are committed to every child within our care reaching their full potential, developing holistically across every area of their lives both now and in their future. All of this is underpinned by our philosophy of education which highlights our focus on inspirational leadership, deep learning and healthy communities. It aspires to develop the character and competence of every child within every community of which we are a part.
At Oasis Community Learning therefore, we believe we are all ‘the architects of our students’ lives’ and as such we are committed to laying the right foundations for every one of our young people.
We also know that great schools are only sustainable within happy and healthy communities. In order to tackle the root causes of disadvantage we seek to ensure that school improvement and community development go hand in hand. In this way, the improvement is likely to be deeper, mutually supporting and long lasting.
Our academies are therefore just a part of an Oasis ‘Hub’ that provides wide-ranging and integrated services, designed to meet the needs of local people. Our shared aim is to work with and alongside disadvantaged children, young people, whole families and members of the wider community, empowering them to transform their neighbourhoods into places that are safe, supportive and full of opportunity. We want to see no one excluded or isolated, inclusive communities where every individual is supported to thrive and flourish. Find out more about Hub and what we do for our communities.
So we look forward to your family potentially becoming part of Oasis, in the knowledge that we will work in partnership with you to ensure your children become confident learners ready to fulfil their aspirations in life.
John Barneby
Chief Executive Officer, Oasis Community Learning

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from our Founder - Oasis Community Learning
pageCache.text:
Exceptional Education at the Heart of the Community
Welcome from our Founder
When I started Oasis back in 1985, I had no idea it would grow into the wonderful family of charities that it has become today.
In Oasis Community Learning, we are one of the country’s largest providers of academy schools, educating over 32,000 children and young people every year. Through Oasis Community Housing, we provide housing for vulnerable young people. With Oasis Community Partnerships we run social projects – from community farms and coffee houses to churches and children’s centres – and much more besides. We do this in communities as diverse as Gateshead in the North East to Bristol in the South West. And through Oasis Restore, another part of Oasis, we aim to transform the lives of young offenders by running the country’s first ever secure school, with a key focus on holistic care and education.
So, the question is…why?
Not only do we believe everyone in our family should receive the very best formal education, but also that there is more to a healthy life and future than simply the knowledge they hold. Every one of us is a product of the community we live in. That is why we are passionate that every community served by one of our academies should be a happy, healthy place where every person is included and valued, and can thrive and achieve their full, God-given potential. That is why Oasis’ vision not only aims to deliver exceptional education, but also to help build great local inclusive neighbourhoods.
We are motivated by our core Christian ethos which means that we believe every person – those of all faiths or none – are equally valuable and have a part to contribute in helping this vision become a reality. Helping a young person realise who they are meant to be is about more than simply the qualifications they get or the job they want; it’s about how they see themselves and those around them. It’s about understanding the role they have as active citizens in our shared world. That’s why Oasis’ goal is to help every young person achieve their best, respect themselves, value those around them and contribute to the good of all.
We look forward to meeting you and welcoming you into an Oasis academy in order to experience this for yourself.
Steve Chalke, MBE
Founder, Oasis

pageCache.pageTitle: Working in Partnership with Unions at Oasis Community Learning - Oasis Community Learning
pageCache.text:
Exceptional Education at the Heart of the Community
Working in Partnership with Unions at Oasis Community Learning
At Oasis, we believe that every voice matters and that includes the collective voice of our people through their trade unions. We are proud to have a strong, positive and constructive relationship with recognised teaching and support staff unions, including NASUWT, NEU, Unison, GMB, ASCL, Unite, NAHT and Community.
We see unions as valued partners in shaping the kind of workplace where everyone can grow, thrive, and be treated with fairness and respect. Together, we:
· Listen and act on staff feedback through regular meetings with union representatives.
· Collaborate on policy to improve working conditions, wellbeing, and workload management.
· Support individual members with access to representation when needed.
· Work together on equality and inclusion, ensuring all voices are heard and valued.
This partnership isn’t just on paper, it’s embedded in our culture. Union representatives are active in our schools, meet regularly with leaders, and take part in health and safety committees and consultation on organisational change.
Why this matters for you
When you join Oasis, you’re joining a community where:
· You have the freedom to join a recognised union if you choose.
· Your union representatives have direct access to senior leaders at school, regional and national levels.
· There is a genuine commitment to open dialogue, shared problem-solving, and mutual respect.
Our shared successes
Our history of working closely with unions includes navigating the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic together, introducing flexible working arrangements, improving leave entitlements, and strengthening wellbeing and safety measures. These achievements reflect our ongoing belief that we are stronger together.
A workplace where your voice counts.
Whether through your line manager, our staff networks, or your union representative, we want you to feel heard, supported, and able to thrive. That’s the Oasis way.

Our People Statement of Intent
Over the last forty years Oasis has built a movement and a culture founded by our people built on our relationships, vision, and ethos.
Our People Statement of Intent was created by listening to everyone across our movement. It sets out the aspiration we have for our people and establishes what it means to be part of Oasis.
We talked to our staff and volunteers up and down the country about what it is like to be part of Oasis and what we want it to be like for everyone in the family.
Based on our organisational vision and values, and supplemented by feedback from our people, we recognise that:
Our 5 people priorities
The People Statement of Intent enshrines 5 people priorities.
As part of Oasis, you are part of a movement that is seeking to change the world. You will have opportunities to delve into how your role contributes to achieving the Oasis vision and mission.
As part of Oasis, we all have opportunities to grow our shared culture and engage in our journey of personal development.
As part of Oasis, you will experience interest in all aspects of your individual development and be able to encourage the development of those around you. ​
As part of Oasis, we experience a sense of wholeness and wellbeing together and as such we will take good care of ourselves, and model this to others​.
You will experience opportunity, support, and accountability as part of your role. We share your passion about our work, and how we inspire one another to do our best.
